QuickFlow

A transparent Rational Method check for peak runoff.

Calculated in your browser
0–1
ha
mm/h

Use the project’s design storm and appropriate duration. No rainfall data is fetched.

Peak runoff83.33L/s

0.08333 m³/s

Q = C × i × A ÷ 360 (m³/s)

Area in hectares. Intensity in mm/h.
The output is peak flow, not storage volume.

Method, assumptions & source

The unit conversion is exact: 1 mm/h over 1 ha = 1/360 m³/s. The Rational Method applies the runoff coefficient to that flow. Published equations often round this factor to 0.00278.

Choose the rainfall duration, design event, climate allowance and coefficient using the project’s applicable standards. This tool does not assess method suitability, time of concentration, routing, detention, blockage or downstream capacity.

Method reference: NZTA Stormwater Treatment Standard (2010), Rational Method. Confirm current project requirements separately.

GradeCheck

Level difference, grade and 1-in-N slope. The direction is explicit.

Calculated in your browser

m

Use the horizontal distance, rather than the sloping pipe length.

Grade in the entered direction1.25%

1 in 80 · 1.25 m fall

Grade (%) = (start − end) ÷ length × 100

A positive grade falls from start to end.

Method & assumptions

Fall = start level − end level. Grade = fall / horizontal length × 100. The 1-in-N ratio is horizontal length / absolute level difference.

A negative grade rises in the entered direction. A zero difference is level and has no finite 1-in-N ratio. This is geometry only; hydraulic capacity, minimum grades, cover, tolerances and network requirements need separate checks.

Surplus after meeting fill demand

Reusable cut (bank m³)1,080
Fill demand (bank m³)1,000
Unsuitable cut (bank m³)120
Total export (loose m³)240

Export includes surplus reusable and unsuitable cut, using the entered bulking factor for both.

Volume basis & assumptions

Available cut = bank cut × reusable proportion. Required bank material = compacted fill / compacted yield. Their difference is the reusable bank-volume balance.

For export, surplus reusable cut and unsuitable cut are converted to loose volume using the entered bulking factor. A deficit is an import requirement stated in bank-equivalent m³; it is not a loose truck volume.

Choose factors from appropriate geotechnical and construction information. This is a preliminary mass-balance aid, assuming a single material and a common bulking factor. It excludes topsoil, stripping, settlement, waste handling, staging and material-specific density changes.

How to use the brief

Supply the relevant project documents and verified standards within your organisation’s approved environment. Check the generated observations, references and actions yourself before relying on them.

Your typed context is not put into share links or saved by this site. No AI API is called. A generated prompt cannot establish technical compliance.

Preliminary checks and workflow prototypes. Confirm inputs, applicability and outputs before project use. Inputs remain in this browser; calculation share links include the numeric inputs you choose to share.
